Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the RetailFlow Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for those wishing to ask a question will be given later. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to RetailFlow Inc.'s Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Lee, CEO; Taylor Kim, CFO; Morgan Patel, COO; Sarah Chen, CMO; Riley Novak, CTO; and Jordan Quinn, CDO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, CEO of RetailFlow Inc.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by the outstanding effectiveness of our marketing campaigns in elevating brand awareness and accelerating customer acquisition, alongside the powerful impact of our promotional activities that boosted sales volumes while carefully managing profitability trade-offs. We saw significant growth in key metrics, including a 32% year-over-year increase in net new customers to 4.2 million and gross merchandise value climbing to $2.8 billion.

Our focus remains on rolling out innovative new products and services, where we're seeing promising early traction and positive customer feedback. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our NovaAI Personal Shopper app, EcoThread subscription boxes, and HyperDash same-day delivery network, which we believe will significantly enhance customer engagement, recurring revenue, and fulfillment efficiency.

We are investing heavily in expanding our seller ecosystem and value-added services to drive higher monetization.

We are focused on improving our gross margins through mix shifts and supply chain optimizations.

We are expanding our presence with more active sellers and deeper revenue per seller.

Finally, we are committed to delivering robust net income and EPS that exceed expectations, reflecting our operational discipline.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our Q2 2024 revenue was $1.8 billion, an increase of 28% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.5%, driven by a favorable product mix shift toward higher-margin private labels, supply chain efficiencies, and fulfillment optimizations that offset promotional pressures and freight cost headwinds. Operating expenses were $720 million, representing 40% of revenue. Our marketing spend was disciplined, with efficiencies from AI-driven targeting contributing to a 14% reduction in customer acquisition costs.

Our net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $1.12 per share. This marked an 18% year-over-year increase and beat consensus expectations of $240 million in net income and $0.98 EPS by solid margins. The outperformance stemmed from top-line momentum in GMV up 25% to $2.8 billion, take rate expansion, and cost controls, including savings from new micro-fulfillment centers. We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of $7.0-7.2 billion in revenue and EPS of $4.55-$4.75.

Let me expand on some key drivers. Starting with gross margin trends, we achieved 42.5%, up 150 basis points year-over-year and 50 basis points sequentially. This builds on three straight quarters of expansion after 2022's inflation and supply disruptions eroded margins. Higher-margin home essentials and owned beauty brands now make up 28% of GMV, while private labels hit 25% of North American sales at 55% margins. Supplier negotiations in apparel hubs like Vietnam yielded 4-6% cost cuts, and AI bidding platforms trimmed landed costs by 3.2%. Fulfillment costs dropped 7% with in-house handling at 65% of volume and robotics boosting pick rates 35%. Headwinds included 60 basis points from shipping inflation and 40 from promos, but dynamic pricing limited damage. Regionally, North America led at 44.2%, Europe at 39.8% despite VAT issues, and APAC at 41.5% with local sourcing. We're targeting 45%+ margins long-term via GenAI supply chain tools and owned inventory growth to 30% of GMV.

Promotional activities were central to our sales surge, pushing GMV to $2.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year, with 45 million orders and 1.2 billion sessions. BFCM and flash sales drove 60% of traffic lift, with A/B tests showing 4.2x ROAS. AOV held at $62 but basket size rose 12% via bundling. Conversion hit 4.8% peaks from AI recs. North America grew 42%, APAC 55% via Singles' Day ties. Margins dipped 180 basis points to 28.5% from low-margin category shifts and 22% average discounts, but vendor-funded promos recovered 100 basis points. Operating income rose 15% to $420 million, CAC payback shortened to 4.2 months, and loyalty enrollment hit 12 million. Dynamic pricing and GenAI bundles enhanced efficiency, with tiered offers cutting cannibalization 15%. Q3 promos should drive 18-22% GMV at stabilizing 29% margins.

On seller performance, we hit 1.28 million active sellers, up 32% year-over-year, with 8% sequential growth. SMBs grew 35%, top 10,000 driving 42% GMV. Revenue per seller reached $3,420 annualized, up 18%, from 14.2% take rates and 22% ad spend hikes. The Seller Ignition Program added 45,000 net new, churn fell to 4.2% via AI dashboards, and cross-border sales hit 22%. North America at $4,100 per seller, APAC up 48% in adds. We're guiding to 1.45 million sellers and $3,700 revenue per by year-end, fueled by OmniAI Suite.

Seller services and value-added services revenue hit $4.2 billion, 28% of total and up 52% year-over-year. Adoption reached 72% of 2.8 million actives, with fulfillment at 41%, ads at 55%, payments 62%. ARPU rose 31% to $1,850 monthly, contribution margins 78%. Ads led at $2.1 billion, logistics $1.3 billion. VAS drove 35% of revenue growth, with multi-service users at 42% seeing 2.5x GMV lift. GenAI SmartStore and GlobalRoute optimizations boosted uptake. North America 78% adoption, APAC 72% growth. Q3 guide $4.5-4.7 billion.

New launches contributed meaningfully: NovaAI added $45 million GMV with 22% conversion lift and NPS 72; EcoThread 250k subs at 25% margins, NPS 68; HyperDash 500k orders at $4.20 cost, NPS 75. These drove 8% GMV growth, services mix to 22%.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Patel to discuss operations.

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. Operationally, we focused on fulfillment network expansion and last-mile innovations like HyperDash, alongside inventory optimization. Our shipping times improved by 25% to under 2 days on average. Fulfillment costs were down 12% year-over-year to $3.45 per unit, thanks to robotics and 12 new micro-centers. We are implementing AI routing via GlobalRoute, cutting dwell times 40% and boosting on-time rates to 98%.

Now I'll turn it over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Morgan. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from the Flow Forward campaign and TikTok Shop integrations. Customer acquisition costs were $42, down 14%. Our brand awareness increased by 18% in unaided recall to 32% among 18-34s per NielsenIQ. We are focusing on omnichannel synergy and sustainability messaging.

To elaborate, our campaigns powered 28% revenue growth to $1.2 billion. Brand tracking showed 18% unaided recall surge to 32%, aided at 68%, ahead of Zara. Flow Forward's $150 million spend hit 2.8 billion impressions: 45% paid social, 30% CTV, 25% DOOH. TikTok VTR 25%, 1.2 million UGC posts. North America up 22% via NFL, EMEA 15% influencers, APAC 35% KOLs.

Customer adds 4.2 million, 32% up, CAC $42 vs. $58 median. Paid social 58% at 6.8x ROAS, Google 22% 4.9x, organic 15%. AOV $68, LTV/CAC 4.1x. Server-side tracking hit 95% accuracy, AI personalization lifted conversions 19%. Value messaging resonated in LatAm 45% growth. Insights: omnichannel 28% cross-retarget, sustainability 25% lift, A/B testing 15% CTR gain. Q3 $200 million spend targets 5 million adds.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Novak.

Riley Novak:
Thanks, Sarah. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization like NovaAI and dynamic pricing engines, plus website scalability. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 35%. We're investing in edge AI and GenAI for AR try-ons and seller tools like SmartStore.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Quinn.

Jordan Quinn:
Thanks, Riley. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 22% improvement in conversion rates because of our AI personalization and predictive analytics initiatives. We are also focusing on first-party data unification and privacy enhancements via our CDP, ensuring GDPR/CCPA compliance with 75% consent rates.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Emily Zhang with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Zhang:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you expand on the new product launches like NovaAI and EcoThread—early metrics and feedback?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Emily. Absolutely. NovaAI Personal Shopper, our GenAI app, saw 1.2 million downloads, 45% retention, DAUs 350k, and 22% conversion lift to $68 AOV, adding $45 million GMV. NPS 72, with users loving the stylist feel, though we iterated on sizing via RLHF. EcoThread boxes hit 250k subs, 35% MoM adds, $28 million run-rate at 25% margins, NPS 68 for the eco-angle. HyperDash delivered 500k orders at 98% on-time. US strong, Europe regulatory-adjusted, APAC explosive. These are scaling our services to 22% of revenue.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rossi with JPMorgan.

Mike Rossi:
Great, thanks. Taylor, on gross margins and promos—how are you balancing the sales lift with profitability?

Taylor Kim:
Hi Mike. Promos drove the GMV surge but pressed margins 180 bps to 28.5%, offset by VFPs and efficiencies. Gross margin expanded overall to 42.5% via private labels at 55%, supplier cuts 4-6%, robotics down 7% fulfillment costs. Shipping headwinds 60 bps mitigated by thresholds. We're value engineering tiered offers, targeting 29% stabilization. Long-term, GenAI demand sensing for 45%+ margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Morgan, operational details on seller fulfillment and costs?

Morgan Patel:
Sure, Lisa. Active sellers leveraging FBM at 41% adoption, units up 65% to 450 million. Costs down 12% with 250 centers at 92% utilization, robotics 35% faster picks. GlobalRoute ML cut costs 18%, Prime on-time 95%. Ties into VAS growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Barclays.

David Patel:
Hi team. Sarah, more on marketing ROI and brand metrics?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks David. Flow Forward impressions 2.8 billion, share of voice 14%, recall 32% unaided. Acqs 4.2 million, CAC $42, ROAS 6.8x TikTok. AI personalization 19% conversion lift, LTV/CAC 4.1x. Regional wins: NA NFL, APAC KOLs. Q3 targets 35% recall.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Lee with Citi.

Sophia Lee:
Thanks. Riley, tech investments in AI and new launches?

Riley Novak:
Hi Sophia. NovaAI fine-tuned on 5 years data, <200ms latency via AWS Outposts. Seller AI pricing lifts 8-12%, GlobalInsights reduces stockouts 22%. Uptime 99.99%, app +35%. $50M FY edge AI for AR, competing walled gardens.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with Deutsche Bank.

Alex Kim:
Thanks. Jordan Q, data role in conversions and privacy?

Jordan Quinn:
Thanks Alex. AI recs drove 22% conversion gains, CDP unifies signals for 95% attribution. Privacy: 75% opt-ins, server-side tracking cookieless-ready. Predictive churn 87% accurate, boosting repeats 15%.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jordan Lee for closing remarks.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
